topPRs.title: feat: Osaki Sepolia L1 + L2 ProxyAdmin owner transfers (097, 098)
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Two stacked tasks that move the **Osaki Sepolia** (chainId `9111973`) chain
ownership from the standard Sepolia L1PAO Safe to the new owner Safe
`0xFB0F8937A0d6999C67E8a01310eBf7fe1859205F` (and its L1-to-L2 alias on L2).

- **`097-osaki-l1-ownership-transfers`** — `TransferOwners` template
  - `ProxyAdmin.transferOwnership(0xFB0F...)`
  - `DisputeGameFactoryProxy.transferOwnership(0xFB0F...)`
  - `DelayedWETH` (v1.5.0) is post-U16 / not ownable → the template logs a
    "not ownable, not performing transfer" line and produces no state change.
- **`098-osaki-l2pao-transfer`** — `TransferL2PAOFromL1` template
  - `OptimismPortal.depositTransaction` targeting the L2 ProxyAdmin predeploy
    (`0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000018`) with
    `transferOwnership(alias(0xFB0F...))`.
  - Aliased L2 owner: `0x0C208937a0D6999c67E8A01310ebF7fE18593170`.
  - Stacked after `097`. A `stateOverride` pre-applies the L1 transfer so the
    template's `proxyAdmin.owner() == newOwnerToAlias` check passes when
    simulating in isolation.

Osaki is not in the public `superchain-registry`; both tasks use
`fallbackAddressesJsonPath` with chain addresses sourced from `op-deployer`
state. The chain reuses OP Sepolia's standard `SuperchainConfig`
(`0xC2Be75506d5724086DEB7245bd260Cc9753911Be`), so
`TransferOwners._validateSuperchainConfig` is satisfied.

The L1PAO is a 2-of-2 nested Safe (FoundationUpgradeSafe + SecurityCouncil).
All three Safe nonces are pinned via `stateOverrides` so the domain/message
hashes in each `VALIDATION.md` are reproducible — signers must re-verify the
live nonces with `cast call <safe> "nonce()"` before signing and bump the
overrides + re-simulate if anything has advanced.

## Test plan

Both tasks simulate cleanly on Sepolia:

- [x] `just simulate foundation` for 097 and 098 produces the hashes recorded
      in each `VALIDATION.md`.
- [x] `just simulate council` for 097 and 098 produces the hashes recorded in
      each `VALIDATION.md`.
- [x] `just simulate-stack sep 097-osaki-l1-ownership-transfers <foundation|council>`
      passes the TaskManager hash check.
- [x] `just simulate-stack sep 098-osaki-l2pao-transfer <foundation|council>`
      passes the TaskManager hash check (stack: 097 → 098).
- [x] Observed L1 state diff for 097: ProxyAdmin slot `0x00` and
      DisputeGameFactoryProxy slot `0x33` flip from the old to the new owner.
- [x] Observed L1 state diff for 098: OptimismPortalProxy params slot bump
      with `_gasLimit = 0x30d40 (200,000)`; L2 effect is verified post-
      execution per the manual steps in `098/VALIDATION.md`.

## Pre-signing checklist (for reviewers)

- [ ] Confirm `0xFB0F...205F` is the intended new owner (verified on-chain as
      a 1-of-12 Gnosis Safe v1.4.1).
- [ ] Confirm DGF + ProxyAdmin should be transferred together (DelayedWETH is
      non-ownable and skipped automatically).
- [ ] Re-verify the three live Safe nonces against `cast call <safe> "nonce()"`
      and update the `stateOverrides` + re-simulate if any have advanced
      since the values pinned in `config.toml`.

topPRs.title: feat: support Tenderly's new ?draft= simulation link format
topPRs.author: sbvegan
topPRs.body:
## Context

Tenderly shipped a breaking change to how the Simulator hydrates a pre-filled form from a URL ([Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C053NFWLG9K/p1781002848689189)). The old query-param format we emitted (`?network=…&contractAddress=…&from=…&stateOverrides=…&rawFunctionInput=…`) **no longer applies state overrides or gas** — signers had to re-enter everything by hand, defeating the purpose of the printed link.

The [new format](https://tenderlydev.notion.site/Simulator-draft-links-draft-37b84be6a2e680bb9874f18a833c1997) encodes the whole simulation as a single JSON payload, base64url-encoded (no padding), in a `?draft=` query parameter:

```
https://dashboard.tenderly.co/<org>/<project>/simulator/new?draft=<base64url(json)>
```

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "network": { "id": "<chainid>" },
  "row": {
    "contractAddress": "<to>",
    "from": "<from>",
    "inputDataType": "raw",
    "rawFunctionInput": "<calldata>",
    "gas": "<TENDERLY_GAS>",
    "stateOverrides": [ { "contractAddress": "0x…", "balance": "", "storage": [ { "key": "0x…", "value": "0x…" } ] } ]
  }
}
```

## What changed

- **`src/libraries/MultisigTaskPrinter.sol`** — new `getTenderlySimulationLink(...)` builds the draft JSON `row`/payload and encodes it with the already-imported solady `Base64.encode(data, /*fileSafe*/ true, /*noPadding*/ true)`. `printTenderlySimulationData` now emits the draft link instead of the old query-param URL. (`Simulation.logSimulationLink` in the `base-contracts` submodule is left untouched; its only remaining callers are archived rehearsal scripts.)
- **Length fallback** — Tenderly's new format caps usable links at ~2000 chars (the old cap was 7980). Since real tasks wrap a Safe `execTransaction` (large calldata), the link is built **without** `rawFunctionInput` and the calldata is printed separately under `Insert the following hex into the 'Raw input data' field:` for manual paste. This mirrors the prior long-URL behavior and is the common path for production tasks.
- **`test/libraries/TenderlySimulationLink.t.sol`** — unit tests pinning the exact draft payload for the inline-calldata, no-raw-input (fallback), and no-gas paths, plus a guard that the legacy `network=`/`stateOverrides=%5B` params are gone.
- **Docs** — `runbooks/key-handover.md` and `docs/simulate-l2-ownership-transfer.md` updated to the new format.

## How it was tested

**Unit tests** (deterministic; env-sensitive assertions kept in one function to avoid the shared-`TENDERLY_GAS` race):
```
forge test --match-path "test/libraries/TenderlySimulationLink.t.sol" -vv
```

**Live Sepolia simulations** (against a real RPC):
- **Single task** — `086-U19-op-betanet-permissioned`, forked at block `10971228` (one before its on-chain execution tx, since 086 is already EXECUTED). Printed a valid draft link + fallback hex.
- **Stacked tasks** — the PR #1440 stack `[099-U19-op-ink-mmz-soneium, 100-U19-unichain]` via `just simulate-stack sep 100-U19-unichain`. Both tasks printed valid draft links.

Each produced link was base64url-decoded and confirmed to be valid JSON with the correct `v`/`network.id`/`contractAddress`/`from`/`gas`/`stateOverrides`.

> Note on stacked links: a downstream task's link can't reproduce the *chain-state* mutations made by earlier tasks in the stack (only Safe threshold/owner/nonce travel in the overrides). This is the pre-existing "stacked Tenderly links may not work" limitation the `simulate-stack` recipe already warns about — not introduced by this change.

## How a reviewer can validate

1. **Run the unit tests:** `forge test --match-path "test/libraries/TenderlySimulationLink.t.sol" -vv` (4 cases, should pass).
2. **Simulate a task** and inspect the printed `Simulation link:` — confirm it is a `…/simulator/new?draft=<b64url>` URL (no legacy query params).
3. **Decode the draft** to confirm the payload is correct:
   ```bash
   python3 -c 'import base64,json,sys; d=sys.argv[1]; print(json.dumps(json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(d+"="*(-len(d)%4))),indent=2))' "<paste the value after ?draft=>"
   ```
   Expect `v:1`, `network.id` = the chain id, and the right `contractAddress`/`from`/`gas`/`stateOverrides`.
4. **Open the link in Tenderly** (replacing `TENDERLY_USERNAME`/`TENDERLY_PROJECT` with your own org/project, or set the `TENDERLY_*` env vars before simulating) and confirm the form pre-fills network, contract, from, gas, and state overrides. For large-calldata tasks, paste the separately-printed hex into "Raw input data".

topPRs.title: docs: add AGENTS.md AI agent guidance
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds a root-level `AGENTS.md` with AI-agent (and human) guidance for working in
this repo, focused on the safety constraints around governance operations.

This is part of an ongoing migration of AI guidance out of an internal tooling
plugin and into the repos it applies to, so the guidance lives as committed,
reviewable docs alongside the code it governs.

## What was migrated

Governance/task guidance previously held in the internal plugin has been
distilled into a single self-contained `AGENTS.md`. It captures:

- What this repo is (tasks, templates, validation files, simulation) and its
  layout (`src/tasks/eth`, `src/tasks/sep`, `src/template`, etc.).
- The non-negotiable safety constraints: every task ships `config.toml` +
  `README.md` + `VALIDATION.md`; calldata must be independently verifiable;
  simulations must pass against forked state before signing; every address is
  verified against the Superchain Registry; timelocks documented and respected.
- Author / review workflows that point to the existing canonical `docs/` guides
  rather than duplicating them.

The content was reconciled against the repo's actual structure (e.g. `src/tasks/`
and `cd src/ && just test`, not the stale paths the plugin carried), and links
to `docs/NEW_TASK_GUIDE.md`, `docs/NEW_TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md`, the SINGLE/NESTED
execution + validation docs, and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Source → destination mapping

| Source (internal plugin) | Destination |
|--------------------------|-------------|
| governance rules (task constraints, review workflow) | `AGENTS.md` → safety constraints + review sections |
| governance domain knowledge (concepts, process, safety) | `AGENTS.md` → key concepts + author task sections |
| superchain-ops repo knowledge (layout, build/test, conventions) | `AGENTS.md` → repository layout + build/test sections |

## Why `AGENTS.md` at the root

The repo had no `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or `docs/ai/` directory. `AGENTS.md` is
the standard home for agent instructions and does not conflict with the existing
human-facing `docs/` tree, which it references rather than duplicates.

## Notes

- Internal tooling mechanics (skill names, internal review-agent steps, plugin
  paths) were intentionally dropped — only repo-applicable technical guidance was
  migrated.
- Draft for review; not ready to merge.

topPRs.title: fix(SetDisputeGameImpl): zero initBonds(8) on CANNON_KONA disable path
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
## Summary

The kona disable branch in `SetDisputeGameImpl._setKonaImplementation` (`impl == 0`) cleared `gameImpls[CANNON_KONA]` and `gameArgs[CANNON_KONA]` but left `initBonds[CANNON_KONA]` untouched. Two compounding causes:

1. The disable branch **early-returns** before the bond-setting block (`return;` at the old line 150).
2. The bond-setting block was guarded by `k.bond != 0` — i.e. `bond = 0` in TOML is the "skip" sentinel used across this template (see [091/config.toml:52](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/blob/main/src/tasks/sep/091-alpha-set-dispute-game-impl-permissionless/config.toml#L52) for the same convention on PDG). So even without the early-return, you could not zero a bond from the TOML.

The post-disable validator (`_validateKona`) also only asserted that `gameArgs` was empty, so a residual `initBonds[CANNON_KONA]` passed simulation cleanly.

## Live evidence

Observed today on **karst-u19-beta-0** (Sepolia, DGF `0x313bcDa9f2D76Bab3554436a434A41779dAC74d0`) after [task 095](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/tree/main/src/tasks/sep/095-beta-0-zero-cannon-kona-game-type) ran:

| field | observed | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `gameImpls(8)` | `0x0` | `0x0` ✅ |
| `gameArgs(8)` | `0x` | `0x` ✅ |
| `initBonds(8)` | **`80000000000000000` (0.08 ETH)** | **`0`** ❌ |

The slot is inert (no one can call `create(8, …)` with `gameImpls(8) == 0`), so this is *functionally* harmless. But it's dead state that diverges from the disable path's intent and from what the task config thought it was producing (the task set `bond = 0` in the kona section assuming that meant \"set to zero\" — it meant \"skip\").

## The fix

- `_setKonaImplementation` disable branch: require `k.bond == 0` in the supplied config (consistency with the existing `k.gameArgs.length == 0` requirement), and call `factory.setInitBond(CANNON_KONA, 0)` when the on-chain bond is non-zero (idempotent otherwise).
- `_validateKona` disable case: also require `factory.initBonds(CANNON_KONA) == 0`.

Both changes are scoped to the disable path; the wire/update path is unchanged.

## Out of scope (worth follow-ups)

- The same \"`bond = 0` means skip\" sentinel applies to `_setInitBonds` for FDG and PDG (`SetDisputeGameImpl.sol:188-195`). If anyone ever wants to zero an FDG/PDG bond via this template, the same gap exists there. I left it untouched because there's no live evidence of it biting, and changing the semantics of `fdgBond/pdgBond = 0` would be a behaviour break for existing in-flight tasks (e.g. 091, 095, 096 all use it as a deliberate \"don't touch\" sentinel).
- The sibling [`SetDisputeGameArgs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/blob/main/src/template/SetDisputeGameArgs.sol#L56) template has a proper `bool setBond` flag that disambiguates \"skip\" from \"set to 0\". If/when we migrate kona-disable tasks to `SetDisputeGameArgs`, that's the cleaner long-term home.

## Cleanup for beta-0 itself

This PR doesn't retroactively zero the residual bond on beta-0; that needs a one-shot tx (e.g. via `SetDisputeGameArgs` with `{chainId=420110023, gameType=8, impl=0x0, bond=0}` once that template is taught to call `setInitBond(_, 0)` on disable, or a direct `factory.setInitBond(8, 0)` PAO Safe tx). Filing separately.

## Test plan

- [x] `forge build src/template/SetDisputeGameImpl.sol --skip test` — compiles clean
- [ ] Existing regression tests (`testRegressionCallDataMatches_SetDisputeGameImpl{,_Kona}`) — they exercise only the wire/update path (impl != 0), so behaviour is unchanged. (Couldn't run them locally — pinned forks need archive RPC; CI will.)
- [ ] Consider adding a new example task under `test/tasks/example/sep/` that exercises the kona disable path so the regression suite picks it up going forward.
